title: The scalar/tensor comparison is uniquely fixed on K-flat representatives.
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme in universe $u$ [def-pc-scheme], let $A,B$ be commutative rings in universe $u+1$, and let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a unital ring homomorphism. Work with ordinary module-valued sheaves on the small etale site, and their unbounded derived categories $D_A,D_B$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Write $Q_A,Q_B$ for cochain localization. Use the existing sheafified scalar adjunction $E\dashv U$, exact derived restriction $DU$, and the published chosen adjunction $L\dashv DU$ [def-sp-coefficient-scalar-representatives]. Thus $L$ is the functor called scalarExtension in the published interface. Put $S=U(\mathbf1_B)$, and let $S[0]\in D_A$ be the degree-zero complex. The tensor products are the sheafified ordinary tensor and its fixed K-flat derived tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product; def-kun-derived-tensor].

For an $A$-module sheaf $M$, let $\tau_M:M\otimes_A S\to UEM$ be the ordinary scalar unit $\eta_M$ tensored with $S$, followed by the lax tensorator of $U$ and $U$ of the right unitor. For each cochain complex $P$, let $a_P:L(Q_AP)\to Q_B(EP)$ be the transpose under the chosen adjunction $L\dashv DU$ of $Q_A(\eta_P):Q_AP\to Q_A(UEP)$ followed by the inverse exact-restriction localization comparison [def-sp-coefficient-scalar-representatives]. Define $r_P:DU(L(Q_AP))\to Q_A(UEP)$ by applying $DU$ to $a_P$ and then its exact-localization comparison, including the canonical termwise functor-composition identification. Define
$$c_P:Q_AP\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}S[0]\longrightarrow Q_A(P\otimes_A S)$$
to be the lax tensorator of $Q_A$ on $(P,S[0])$ for the derived monoidal structure of [lem-sfb-derived-monoidal], whose tensor is the fixed derived tensor above, followed by $Q_A$ of the total-tensor/single-complex identification. Here $(P\otimes_A S)^n=P^n\otimes_A S$ with differential $d_P^n\otimes1$; the canonical degree-zero localization identification is understood. Let $\tau_P:P\otimes_A S\to UEP$ be $\tau$ applied degreewise.

There exists exactly one natural isomorphism
$$e:DU\circ L\xrightarrow{\sim}(-\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}S[0]):D_A\longrightarrow D_A$$
such that, for every integer-indexed cochain complex $P$ of $A$-module sheaves,
$$Q_A(\tau_P)\circ c_P\circ e_{Q_AP}=r_P.$$
The tensor functor on the right is precisely the published site-specific derivedTensor functor with second argument scalarCoefficient, identified with scalarTensorModelFunctor by unfolding their definitions. No flatness of $B$ over $A$, boundedness, finiteness, or nonempty-scheme hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Check the category hypotheses before using K-flat derivability. Ordinary $A$-modules form a Grothendieck abelian category [lem-weil-pbc-ring-modules-grothendieck-abelian]; their usual tensor is closed by the explicit currying bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_A(M\otimes_A N,P)=\operatorname{Hom}_A(M,\operatorname{Hom}_A(N,P))$, whose inverse is evaluation. Functorial flat resolutions of abelian groups [lem-sfb-abelian-functorial-flat-resolution] pass to $A$-modules by [lem-sfb-modobj-flat-resolutions], viewing an $A$-module as an internal module in abelian groups. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed] and [lem-sfb-sheaf-functorial-flat-resolution] to the essentially small small-etale site in the coefficient universe $u+1$. Thus $C=\operatorname{Sh}(T_{\mathrm{et}},\operatorname{Mod}A)$ is Grothendieck abelian, closed symmetric monoidal with additive tensor, and has functorial flat resolutions. Tensor preserves colimits by closedness. Apply [lem-sfb-kflat-derivability]: in $K(C)$ the full K-flat subcategory is a left derivability structure, and every complex admits a K-flat resolution. All later localizations and K-flatness refer to this same module-valued category; no comparison with a different coefficient category is used.

proof.text: Prove the ordinary balancing assertion directly, rather than importing the downstream scalar/pullback module: specialize CategoryTheory.isIso_sheafAdjunction_unitProjection to the module scalar adjunction. Restriction preserves sheafification because it has the coextension right adjoint; the module unit projection is invertible by ModuleCat.isIso_extendRestrictScalarsAdj_unitProjection. Thus the published scalarSheafTensorTransformation is a natural isomorphism tau: tensorRight(S) ~= E followed by U, without any flatness assumption. Tensoring an acyclic K-flat complex with S is acyclic (CochainComplex.acyclic_tensorRight_of_kFlat); transport along termwise tau and reflect exactness through faithful scalar restriction. Functor.PreservesKFlatQuasiIso.mk' then proves that E preserves quasi-isomorphisms between K-flat complexes.

proof.text: For a cochain complex P, first form the localization of the ordinary cochain-adjunction unit, composed with the inverse exact-restriction factorization. Naturality of that unit and of the factorization gives a natural transformation eta. Transpose it under the chosen derived scalar adjunction to obtain a natural transformation r, and apply exact restriction and its factorization to obtain r'. By [lem-sfb-exact-right-adjoint-kflat-representative], using the K-flat quasi-isomorphism preservation just proved, the transpose is invertible on K-flat P; hence so is r'. In each degree the cochain-adjunction unit is exactly the published composite of identity and composition identifications with the mapped ordinary unit. Consequently r'_P equals scalarRestrictedExtensionRepresentative(phi,T,P) on every complex, not only K-flat ones.

source.place: Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change, canonical K-flat computation; chosen-adjoint representative as in the existing representative node

proof.text: Put $H(K)=K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}S[0]$. By [lem-sfb-derived-monoidal], the fixed tensor is computed by replacing either argument by a K-flat resolution and its localization is lax monoidal. Consequently its tensorator on $(P,S[0])$ is invertible if $P$ is K-flat; $S$ need not be flat. Compose it with the total-tensor/single identification to obtain exactly $c_P$ of the statement. This identification has in degree $n$ the sole summand $P^n\otimes S$; the second differential is zero and the first is $d_P^n\otimes1$. For a chain map $f$, its degree-$n$ map is $f^n\otimes1$. Lax-tensorator naturality therefore says $Q_A(f\otimes1)c_P=c_{P'}H(Q_Af)$. Thus $\beta_P=Q_A(\tau_P)c_P$ is a natural transformation $HQ_A\Rightarrow Q_AV$, on cochain and homotopy categories, invertible on K-flat objects.

source.place: Tag 06YU, definition-derived-tor and its preceding construction; one-sided K-flat computation as recorded by lem-sfb-derived-monoidal

proof.text: Let F be the termwise functor V=E followed by U, followed by cochain localization. Apply LocalizerMorphism.isLeftDerivedFunctor_of_isLeftDerivabilityStructure on the full K-flat subcategory of cochain complexes. The natural transformations r' and beta constructed above are invertible on every K-flat object, so both (G,r') and (H,beta) are left derived functors of F, by [lem-sfb-unary-left-derived-calculus]. This cochain formulation of the derivability criterion supplies the same universal property on all complexes and avoids a separate descent of the transformations to the homotopy category.

source.place: Tag 06XN, lemma-find-existence-computes, dual criterion; its universal-property formulation in lem-sfb-unary-left-derived-calculus

proof.text: Apply Mathlib Functor.leftDerivedUnique to the two counits r' and beta obtained in Step 5. Its hom component is Functor.leftDerivedNatTrans induced by the identity of the common underived functor, so Functor.leftDerivedNatTrans_app gives e_(Q(P)) followed by beta_P = r'_P. Substitute the proved equality r'_P = scalarRestrictedExtensionRepresentative(phi,T,P). The resulting equation is precisely scalarTensorModelNormalization, and holds for every cochain complex P without cancelling either counit on non-K-flat complexes.

source.place: Universal-property argument for uniqueness of derived functors; Tag 05S9, definition-right-derived-functor, dual, with Tag 06XN

proof.text: For another normalized isomorphism e', both e'.hom and e.hom have the same composite with beta after whiskering by Q, by their all-complex normalization equations. Functor.leftDerived_ext for the tensor left derived functor gives equality of these natural transformations; Iso.ext gives equality of the isomorphisms. Finally transport this unique isomorphism along the inverse of eqToIso(scalarTensorFunctor_eq phi T) to the site-specific derivedTensor endpoint. The two inverse isomorphism identities show both existence with its exact published normalization and uniqueness at that endpoint.

theorem scalarTensorIso_existsUnique
    {A B : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    (φ : A →+* B) (T : Scheme.{u}) :
    ∃! e : scalarExtension φ T ⋙ Sheaf.derivedRestrictScalars T.smallEtaleTopology φ ≅
        (derivedTensor (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) T).flip.obj (scalarCoefficient φ T),
      scalarTensorModelNormalization (scalarCoefficientSheaf φ T)
        (scalarSheafTensorTransformation φ T)
        (e ≪≫ eqToIso (scalarTensorFunctor_eq φ T))
        (scalarRestrictedExtensionRepresentative φ T) := by
  sorry
